messages:
Priya: Quick sync — noticed a sharp CPU + latency bump on dashboard renders for accounts with strict RBAC. Looks like per-tile queries are getting expanded into many small filtered queries when the auth layer kicks in. Anyone else seeing this?
Evan: Yep saw the same on Friday during the loadtest. 95th latency for the dashboard endpoint doubled.
Sam: Do we have a repro that ties the extra fanout to the auth check path vs client-side expansion?
Priya: Repro attached in thread (dev query logs). Short version: query planner issues 6 tile requests, auth layer transforms them into ~18 tenant-filtered queries because of role scoping.
Carla: Oof. That matches a smell I've seen — the auth proxy can't rewrite the tile descriptor into a single RBAC-aware query because it's not in the same execution context. So it splits and issues multiple sub-queries.
Ben: Tradeoff: move RBAC-aware composition into the query layer (server-side) so we can push predicates into a single execution plan vs keep it in the auth service for separation of concerns.
Priya: Proposed intermediate: a thin "composition service" that accepts tile descriptors + a tenant context and returns an execution plan that is RBAC-aware. It would live next to the query layer and call auth only for policy evaluation (not query rewriting). Thoughts?
Alice: I like separating concerns but we need to avoid adding a synchronous hop for every dashboard render. Could we make it colocated with query workers and cache eval results for short TTL?
Evan: Cache helps. Also consider streaming composition: return coarse tiles quickly (best-effort) and asynchronously fill in restricted sub-tiles when policy check completes. That preserves SLOs for 95/99.
Carla: Streaming could be messy for client-side; we'd need a delta protocol or SSE. Also many dashboards expect atomicity for consistency.
Sam: Another option: precompute RBAC-annotated tiles for heavy tenants (materialized per-role). Costy but very fast at read time. Could be a Dedicated-only optimization.
Ben: Agree — multi-pronged: (1) short-term: introduce composition co-located with query workers + TTL policy cache; (2) mid-term: streaming partial renders for non-critical panels; (3) long-term: role-materialized tiles for top customers.
Priya: Implementation sketch: new service "tile-composer" lives on the query plane; accepts {tile_id, tenant_id, role_hash} -> returns a composite SQL/engine plan. It calls policy-eval API (auth) but policy-eval returns normalized constraints instead of issuing queries. Plan generation then compiles to the existing executor. We avoid auth proxy rewriting queries.
Evan: We should add telemetry hooks: counts of plan splits, avg extra sub-queries created, and latency delta attributable to auth evaluation. Also flag when plan splits > 3 so we can auto-suggest materialization.
Alice: For rollout, feature-flag tile-composer per-tenant and start with low-risk dashboards. Add canary on Dedicated where isolation matters.
Carla: Security note: ensure the composer never caches tenant-scoped raw data. Cache only policy results and compiled plans keyed by role_hash+tile_signature. Encrypt memcaches in Private deployments.
Ben: Ops: if composer is colocated with query workers, capacity planning must account for both planning CPU and exec CPU. Might need horizontal autoscale based on plan-rate and exec-rate separately.
Priya: Action items: Sam to prototype composer API and a toy planner; Alice to draft rollout/canary plan; Evan to add telemetry schema; Ben to write capacity guidance; Carla to review security/caching constraints. I can coordinate evals.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new canary cluster for tile-composer created (canary-tiles-03).
Priya: Thanks — ping me in #eng-sre when canary is up so we can run the loadtest. :thumbsup:
Evan: I'll schedule the loadtest for Tuesday 09:00 PT.
Sam: Prototype PR coming by EOD Monday.
Carla: Will review the caching design once PR lands.
Ben: I'll draft a short RFC to capture the design + tradeoffs (server-side composition vs materialization vs streaming).
Priya: Awesome. If anyone has objections to the plan, speak now. Otherwise I'll file the RFC and link it here.
Alice: No objections from me. :+1:
Priya: Filing RFC now — will link once created.
